name: Transcriptional granulocyte commitment with suppressed monocyte-macrophage fate
members: [untitled BTM module] Granulocyte development and activation is the theme here: a transcriptional core that commits myeloid progenitors to the neutrophil lineage, a cytokine receptor that drives their expansion, and signalling and cytoskeletal components that let mature cells respond. PU.1 and the retinoic acid receptor set and maintain myeloid identity, which is why blockade of retinoid signalling in promyelocytic leukaemia arrests cells short of maturity and why pharmacological retinoid treatment restores it.

[untitled BTM module] This grouping describes the transcriptional programme of immature myeloid progenitors in the bone marrow, the stage at which granulocyte, mast cell and erythroid potential is still being resolved and primary granule proteins are first made. Its hallmark products are the azurophilic granule enzymes myeloperoxidase and neutrophil elastase, together with the mast cell protease carboxypeptidase A3 and the promyelocyte membrane marker MS4A3, so the signature marks promyelocytes and their close relatives rather than mature blood cells.

[untitled BTM module] This grouping centres on the housekeeping machinery that keeps mitochondria energetically competent while proteins and metabolites are turned over. Two accessory subunits of respiratory complex I sit alongside the mitochondrial translation elongation factor TUFM, which delivers aminoacyl-tRNAs to the mitoribosome and so supplies the organelle-encoded core of the respiratory chain; PRELID1 participates in phospholipid transfer between mitochondrial membranes, and TMEM160 is an inner-membrane protein.

[untitled BTM module] Membrane traffic and organelle remodelling form the common thread here: newly folded cargo leaves the endoplasmic reticulum in COPII-coated vesicles built from SEC23A and SEC24B, is delivered through early endosomes marked by the tethering factor EEA1, and reaches the plasma membrane by SNARE-directed fusion, with STXBP3 acting among the Sec1/Munc18-family regulators of that step. Lipid composition and cytoskeletal geometry are managed alongside cargo flow: the inositol phosphatase SYNJ1 dephosphorylates PI(4,5)P2 to uncoat vesicles after endocytosis, TMEM30A serves as the accessory subunit that allows P4-ATPase flippases to translocate aminophospholipids across bilayers, and the microtubule-severing ATPase SPAST shapes tubules and axonal microtubule arrays.

[untitled BTM module] This grouping centres on membrane lipid organisation and the trafficking and signalling events built on it. Its clearest core is the aminophospholipid flippase machinery: ATP11B, a P4-ATPase, must partner with the accessory subunit TMEM30A (CDC50A) to fold, reach the plasma membrane and translocate phosphatidylserine to the cytosolic leaflet, which keeps this lipid hidden until apoptosis or platelet activation exposes it.

name: Differentiated intestinal epithelial identity and barrier maintenance
members: [untitled BTM module] These genes together mark the differentiated absorptive epithelium of the intestine, the cell layer that takes up nutrients, senses dietary and xenobiotic chemicals, and forms a barrier to gut contents. Lineage-defining transcription factors such as CDX1 and HNF4G impose regional intestinal identity on gut endoderm and drive expression of the enterocyte's working machinery: a brush border built with the unconventional myosin MYO1A, apical solute carriers including SLC3A1 for cystine and dibasic amino acids and the zinc transporter SLC39A5, and HMGCS2 for ketogenesis from fatty acids in a tissue with high energetic turnover.

[untitled BTM module] These genes mark the differentiated absorptive and secretory epithelium of the gastrointestinal tract, the barrier layer that absorbs nutrients, detoxifies luminal xenobiotics and presents a glycan-coated surface to the microbiota. Adhesion and junctional components such as EPCAM and FERMT1 hold the sheet together, while lineage transcription factors including FOXA3 and KLF5 drive and maintain the differentiated state; loss of these programmes underlies barrier failure, inflammatory bowel disease and the dedifferentiation seen in colorectal cancer, where CEACAM and galectin-4 expression is routinely used as an epithelial marker.

[untitled BTM module] These genes mark the epithelial identity programme of stratified and glandular epithelia, particularly of the gastrointestinal tract, and its coordinated regulation of differentiation, adhesion and mucosal barrier function. Transcription factors set the programme: CDX1 specifies intestinal identity and is a determinant of intestinal metaplasia when expressed in stomach or oesophagus, while KLF5 and the ETS factor EHF drive proliferation and maturation of epithelial progenitors.

[untitled BTM module] These genes define the differentiated intestinal epithelium, the absorptive lineage that lines the small bowel and colon and carries out nutrient uptake, barrier maintenance and fluid balance. The programme is set by a transcription factor core in which CDX1 and CDX2 specify intestinal identity and HNF4A and HNF4G drive enterocyte maturation; loss or ectopic activation of these factors underlies intestinal metaplasia and is used to distinguish gut-derived tumours.
